text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall for REDWOOD-PROD — MULTI-GPU COMMUNICATOR ALERT. Serving cluster serving-prod-3 reporting NCCL rendezvous failures + intermittent CUDA OOMs for model redwood-extended-v2 (tensor-parallel=8, pipeline-parallel=2). Error spike visible since 2024-11-02T02:04:xxZ. Current symptom: requests hitting 503/502 and hanging generations. Estimated impacted requests ~12% across region. Initiating pager. @oncall please pick up.

maya: picking this up. oncall here. seeing: 15% pod restarts in model-pool-redwood-extended-v2. Which pods/nodes are the hottest?

infra-pager: affected nodes: gpunode-12 (10.2.1.45), gpunode-13 (10.2.1.46), gpunode-15 (10.2.1.48). Frequent logs attached below. Rendezvous ID varying across ranks.

infra-pager: ```
[2024-11-02T02:05:12Z] ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled system error, nvmlMemInfo: ok
[2024-11-02T02:05:13Z] NCCL WARN ncclNetTimeout: rank 5 timed out waiting for peer
[2024-11-02T02:05:14Z] cudaMalloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation (out of memory)
[2024-11-02T02:05:15Z] nccl: NCCL ERROR: unhandled system error (0) at /opt/nccl/src/./core.cc:xx
[2024-11-02T02:05:16Z] container restart: exit code 137
```

lucas: looks like a rendezvous race plus some OOMs. tensor/pipeline parallel workloads are sensitive to partial rank failures — if one rank OOMs the rest can hang at allreduce. Any recent rollout that changed batch size or TP config?

sree: I pushed an optimization earlier this morning that raised per-device batch size from 32 -> 48 for a throughput perf test on serving-prod-3 at 01:30 UTC. I thought traffic was low but maybe the test overlapped with live traffic. Rolling back now.

raj: confirm — we saw per-GPU memory pressure spike correlated with that timeframe. Also seeing mismatched rendezvous IDs in logs which implies communicator re-init during an in-flight request. That combination will cause NCCL hangs.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert new traffic off the affected pool -> use routing policy to send 70% to fallback model-variant (quantized-4g single-GPU) and 30% to a canary group, 2) drain gpunode-15 and restart containers there, 3) rollback batch size in model config. Executing step 1 now.

lucas: I'm applying routing override in control plane: `redwoodctl routes set --service redwood-extended-v2 --policy fallback=quant-4g:70,canary:30 --reason "nccl-rendezvous-failure"`

maya: routing override applied. traffic shift observed. latency for fallback variant looks higher but successful.

maya: draining gpunode-15: `kubectl cordon gpunode-15 && kubectl drain gpunode-15 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` — starting restart of pods on that node.

infra-pager: while draining, saw a container runtime error on gpunode-15: journald shows repeated GPU driver soft resets. Suspect intermittent NV driver flaps.

raj: set NCCL debug / env vars to get more info: `export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; export NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL,GPU; export NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1; export NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=2; export NCCL_TIMEOUT=300` — pushing these to canary pods. Also enabling verbose kernel OOM logs.

sree: rolling back my batch size change to 32 in model config and updating autoscaler to prevent burst >40 per-device. Patch: `model-config apply --name redwood-extended-v2 --set device_batch=32`

lucas: also enabling fallback route for any pod restarts — automatic retry policy to move traffic to single-GPU variant if any pod restarts >2 times in 5m.

customer-success-bot: Notifying affected customers: ACME corp and BetaApps saw repeated 5xx between 02:05-02:12 UTC. CS outreach queued.

maya: after drain+restart on gpunode-15, we saw one pod come up with corrected memory footprint. Container restarts stopped on gpunode-15. Monitoring pods on node-12 and node-13 next.

lucas: note — logs show `rendezvous id mismatch` due to partial communicator re-init; I'm forcing a full cluster-wide re-init by restarting the serving pool, one rack at a time. Doing rack-1 now. This will cause transient 503s for small fraction but avoids long hangs.

maya: doing controlled restarts: rack-1 complete, rack-2 start. Observing a drop in NCCL WARN messages.

infra-pager: additional log snippet during restart: ```
[2024-11-02T02:18:41Z] NCCL INFO [-] Creating communicator for ranks [0..7] rendezvous 0xab34ef
[2024-11-02T02:18:43Z] NCCL WARN [-] Rank 6: allreduce stalled, waiting for 1/8 peers
[2024-11-02T02:18:45Z] cudaMalloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation on rank 6
[2024-11-02T02:18:46Z] pod restart triggered; re-init complete
```

raj: we've also bumped the kernel ulimit for user processes and verified no OOM killer invoked at system level. NV driver team notified to correlate with GPU ECC and reset logs.

sree: model-level metrics now show memory usage back to baseline after rollback. Cache (KV cache) re-sync forced to avoid stale keyspace mismatch across ranks: `invalidate-kv-cache --model redwood-extended-v2 --scope pool`

maya: handing incident to eng-runtime for deeper root cause and monitoring for next 45 minutes. @lucas you're owner — I'll remain reachable if traffic changes.

lucas: taking handoff. Current status: routing override active, batch rollback complete, targeted restarts done. Error rate dropped from 12% -> 0.8% over last 8 minutes, tail latency improving. Will keep NCCL_DEBUG logs enabled for 30m and collect rendezvous traces. Creating an incident ticket REDWOOD-INC-2024-334 for postmortem.

customer-success-bot: ACME acknowledged mitigation and closed immediate support ticket; they will await postmortem.

raj: followups: 1) validate autoscaler behavior to prevent test rollout from overlapping with live traffic, 2) investigate NV driver soft resets for gpunode-15 and cross-check firmware, 3) add a guard in runtime to detect partial communicator re-init and fail fast to enable quicker fallback rather than hang.

lucas: agreed — will include recommended config changes in the postmortem. For now I'm watching metrics; will update when NCCL logs are collected.

maya: thanks all. marking paging handoff complete. Monitoring window 30m. If errors climb back above 2% re-page SRE. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigation applied, error rate decreased, handoff to eng-runtime. Next update scheduled in 30m or on change.
